14th July 20XX

Dear Paul,

How are you? I am enjoying my holiday in Vietnam. It is my third day here and we are all having fun. We stayed in a city called Hanoi on Tuesday and Wednesday. On the first day we visited the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. Ho Chi Minh was the most famous leader in Vietnam. He died in 1969 and in 1975, his body was put in the mausoleum. The biggest city of Vietnam also changed its name to Ho Chi Minh City after he died.

I visited the Petrus Ky Mausoleum yesterday too, but there were very few tourists there and it was smaller. Maybe it was because this mausoleum is not as famous as the Ho Chi Minh one.

We also went to a theatre on Wednesday. We saw a brilliant performance of traditional water puppets. The stories and dances were short but they were humorous! I love the music they played during the show too. It was the first time that I have ever seen puppets walk and dance on water. I got a little wet because I sat very close to the water, but I didn’t mind at all. The show was simply amazing!

Today we are in a boat on Halong Bay which is Vietnam's top tourist attraction. Almost every tourist comes here to visit because it is very beautiful. There are over 1,000 stone islands at Halong Bay. Some stones have special shapes. I have seen a stone that looks like a man’s head and another one that looks like a dragon. Some islands have caves on them. Different lights are used so that the caves look colourful. I will take a lot of photos and show you when I get home.

It is our last day here tomorrow. We will go shopping. I hope I can get some souvenirs for my friends.

Bye for now,
Eddie

Andy: Well, I think songs can have an important message for listeners. When I sing, I want to share messages of love, friendship and joy. I hope my songs move people and make them think about their lives.

Reporter: I see. Do you think being a singer is challenging?

Andy: Yes, I do. Not only do you need to sing well, but you also need to be able to entertain your audience so that they’ll enjoy the show. It’s not just singing – it’s show business!

Reporter: Andy, can you give any advice to those who want to be a singer when they grow up?

Andy: Sure. You need to be able to come up with lots of ideas. Creating new songs is a very important part of the job. To entertain your audience, you need to be outgoing. You need to be hard-working too. Some may think it’s easy to become a star and make a fortune. It’s true that I earn a lot now and I can buy anything I want, but it took me many years to become successful. In most cases, it’s all about how much effort you put in.

Reporter: I’m sure that’s true, Andy. Let’s talk about your future plans.

Andy: Well, I’m now working on my new album Fantasy. It features different types of music from love songs to rock songs. I hope it will come out in June this year. I’m also planning a concert in New York next year. It’s time to visit my beloved fans there. I haven’t seen them for ages!

Reporter: Wow, that sounds very exciting! Thanks very much for talking to us today.

Andy: You’re welcome!

samples.title: 熬夜的壞處
samples.passage_text:
「起牀啦！快遲到了！」每天早上，媽媽總是要多番提醒我起牀上學了，而我總是不願起牀，這是因為我熬夜已經習以為常。每天晚上我總是很晚才肯睡覺，第二天上課時總是打瞌睡，根本沒法專注學習，回家後當然不懂得做家課，成績也退步不少。我知道要改變生活習慣，可是沒有決心，爸爸媽媽也束手無策。

一天晚上，為了觀看我期待已久的世界杯球賽，我爬上牀上裝睡，瞞過爸爸媽媽。凌晨一時二十分，我從牀上爬起來，鬼鬼祟祟地走到客廳，打開電視機看球賽。比賽相當激烈，我的心情跟着球隊每一次進攻而起伏，真像坐過山車呢。當看到我喜歡的球隊最終取得冠軍，我激動得差點兒跳了起來，我儘量壓低聲音，回到房間。可能由於心情太興奮，我完全沒有睡意，差不多凌晨五時，我才漸漸睡着。

第二天上學時，我開始有點後悔昨晚熬夜觀看世界杯。我上課一直打瞌睡，眼皮完全不受控制似的，有好幾次我甚至差點趴了在桌子上睡覺。我昏昏欲睡的樣子終於被王老師發現了。

下課後，王老師向我走來，此時我已經做好了被責罵的準備。出乎意料的是，老師沒有教訓我，而是問我是否身體不適。王老師的關心讓我覺得很慚愧，於是我向她坦白昨晚熬夜看比賽的事，才導致今天完全提不起精神。王老師聽完我的話，並沒有指責我，而是告訴我熬夜的壞處，例如影響學習狀態，集中不了精神，免疫力和記憶力下降、影響發育等等。原來熬夜有那麼多壞處，難怪我在日間經常提不起勁。知道熬夜的壞處後，我向王老師保證，以後再也不熬夜了。

我真感激王老師呢！不僅因為她那次「放我一馬」，自那次起，每晚我都盡早完成功課和温習，然後看看電視或做些喜歡的事，確保睡覺的時間不會太晚。現在我每晚都在十點半前睡覺，上課時比以前專注多了，成績自然也進步了不少，爸爸媽媽和老師對於我的進步都感到高興。熬夜有那麼多壞處，我以後也不會熬夜了！

history.title: An Unforgettable Graduation Day
history.passage:
It was June 10th, the day of my primary school graduation ceremony in Hong Kong. I had been looking forward to this day for months, but unfortunately, I woke up feeling terrible. My head was pounding, my throat was sore, and I had a fever.

My mother took my temperature and told me I couldn't go to school. I was devastated. All my classmates would be there, wearing their smartest clothes, receiving their graduation certificates. I had practiced my graduation song so many times, and now I wouldn't be able to sing it with my friends.

Later that afternoon, my best friend Mei Ling called me. She told me all about the ceremony. The principal gave a speech about how proud he was of us. Then, each class performed a song. Mei Ling said they sang our graduation song beautifully, and she thought of me when they sang.

That evening, my teacher Mr. Wong came to visit me at home. He brought my graduation certificate and a special gift from my classmates - a photo album filled with pictures from our time in primary school. Looking through those photos, I realized that even though I missed the ceremony, I would always remember my wonderful friends and teachers.

history.passage:
Many Hong Kong students feel stressed because of their busy schedules. They have to attend school, do homework, and go to extra classes. Some even have music lessons or sports training after school.

Tommy, a Primary 5 student, wakes up at 6:30 every morning. After school, he goes to a tutorial centre for extra English and Maths lessons. At home, he spends two hours on homework every night. On weekends, he has swimming lessons and violin practice.

Tommy’s classmate, Lily, also has a tight schedule. She studies until 10 pm every day. She rarely has time to play with her friends. Both Tommy and Lily feel tired and wish they could have more free time.

Experts say too much stress is bad for children’s health. They suggest students should have at least one hour of playtime every day. Parents and teachers can help by giving students less homework and more time to relax.

history.title: The Secret Life of Ants
history.passage:
Ants are fascinating creatures that live in large colonies. Each ant has a special job to help the group survive. Worker ants gather food, soldier ants protect the nest, and the queen lays eggs.

Ants communicate by releasing chemicals called pheromones. They leave trails to guide others to food sources. When an ant finds food, it returns to the nest while leaving a scent path. Other ants follow this path to collect more food.

Ant colonies can be huge, with thousands of members. They build complex nests underground with many tunnels and chambers. The queen stays in the deepest part, safe from danger. Worker ants constantly expand and repair the nest.

Ants are very strong for their size. They can carry objects many times heavier than themselves. This strength helps them move food and building materials efficiently. Their teamwork makes them one of nature's most successful insects.

history.title: 一場特別的校外教學
history.passage:
今天是五年級校外教學的日子，老師帶我們到郊外的一座生態農場參觀。一開始，農場主人向我們介紹了各種農作物和它們的生長過程，大家都聽得津津有味。

接著，我們分組進行體驗活動。我和同學們一起種下了一些蔬菜種子，並學習如何施肥和澆水。正當我們忙得不亦樂乎時，突然聽到一陣驚呼聲，原來是有人在田邊發現了一隻受傷的小鳥。

history.title: The Secret Garden
history.passage:
One sunny afternoon, Lily discovered a hidden gate in her grandmother's backyard. She pushed it open and found herself in a magical garden filled with colourful flowers, tall trees, and chirping birds. The garden had a small pond with fish swimming happily. Lily felt like she had entered a different world.

She spent hours exploring every corner of the garden. She found a bench under a big tree and sat down to rest. As she looked around, she noticed a tiny birdhouse hanging from a branch. Inside, a family of sparrows had made their home. Lily watched them quietly, feeling peaceful and content.

Before she left, Lily picked a single flower to remember the garden by. She promised herself she would visit again soon. That evening, she told her grandmother about her adventure, but her grandmother just smiled and said, 'Some secrets are meant to be discovered.'

history.passage:
Hong Kong is famous for its bustling city life, but it also has many beautiful scenic spots that are less crowded. One such place is the Tung Ping Chau Island, located in the northeastern part of Hong Kong. This island is part of the Hong Kong UNESCO Global Geopark and is known for its unique rock formations and clear blue waters.

Visitors can take a ferry from Ma Liu Shui Pier to reach Tung Ping Chau. The journey takes about 1.5 hours, but the stunning views along the way make it worthwhile. Once on the island, hiking trails lead to amazing sights like the Kang Lau Shek cliffs and the Lung Lok Shui wave-cut platform. These natural wonders were formed over millions of years by wind and water erosion.

The best time to visit is during spring or autumn when the weather is pleasant. Summer can be very hot, while winter brings strong winds that may cancel ferry services. Remember to bring enough water and sun protection, as there are few shops on the island. With its peaceful atmosphere and breathtaking landscapes, Tung Ping Chau offers a perfect escape from the city's hustle and bustle.

history.title: Exploring Hong Kong's Scenic Spots
history.passage:
Hong Kong is known for its bustling city life, but it also boasts stunning natural landscapes. One hidden gem is the Dragon's Back Trail on Hong Kong Island. This hiking route offers breathtaking views of Shek O Beach and the South China Sea. The trail is named for its undulating ridge that resembles a dragon's spine.

Another must-visit spot is the Tian Tan Buddha on Lantau Island. Standing 34 meters tall, this bronze statue symbolizes harmony between man and nature. Visitors climb 268 steps to reach the base, where they can enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding mountains.

For those interested in geology, the High Island Reservoir features unique hexagonal rock formations created by volcanic activity millions of years ago. These symmetrical columns are best seen during low tide when more of the rocks are exposed.

Each location showcases a different aspect of Hong Kong's natural beauty, from coastal vistas to cultural landmarks and geological wonders. They provide perfect escapes from the urban jungle.

history.title: Reading Comprehension: Scenic Spots in Hong Kong

Hong Kong is famous for its bustling city life, but it also has many beautiful scenic spots. One of these hidden gems is the Dragon's Back trail on Hong Kong Island. This hiking trail offers stunning views of Shek O Beach and the South China Sea. Many visitors are surprised by how peaceful it is, just a short bus ride from the busy city center.

Another lesser-known attraction is the Lai Chi Wo village in the New Territories. This 300-year-old Hakka village has traditional houses surrounded by lush green fields. Visitors can learn about rural life in Hong Kong and see century-old feng shui woods. The village is especially beautiful in spring when the pink coral trees bloom.

For those interested in history, the Lei Cheng Uk Han Tomb Museum is fascinating. This ancient brick tomb from the Han Dynasty was discovered during construction work in 1955. It shows that Hong Kong has been an important place for over 2,000 years. The museum displays pottery and bronze artifacts found in the tomb.

These spots show Hong Kong's diverse attractions beyond shopping malls and skyscrapers. They offer glimpses into the city's natural beauty and rich history that many tourists miss.
